title: Etale locality of punctual cohomological purity
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

Let $f:Y\to X$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] between regular Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. For every $y\in Y$ and $x=f(y)$, $Y$ is punctually pure at $y$ if and only if $X$ is punctually pure at $x$. Consequently, $X$ is punctually pure if and only if every member $Y_\alpha$ of any jointly surjective family of etale morphisms $Y_\alpha\to X$ with regular Noetherian $Y_\alpha$ is punctually pure. Jointly surjective means that every point of $X$ belongs to the image of at least one $Y_\alpha$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2 and the strict-henselization invariance stated after Definition 3.2.1, printed p.244; applied to etale neighbourhoods in the concluding reduction from Proposition 3.6.5 to Theorem 3.6.2, printed p.253.

proof.text: Choose affine neighbourhoods $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Y$, $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset X$ of $y,x$ with $C\to B$ etale, as allowed by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $R=C_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $S=B_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. By [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension], $\dim R=\dim S=d$. The residue extension $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ is finite separable by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable]. Choose compatible embeddings into a separable closure $k^s$ of $\kappa(x)$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ containing it. Then $k^s$ is also a separable closure of $\kappa(y)$. Apply [lem-sc-etale-triple-strict-henselization-identification] to the etale $R$-algebra $B\otimes_C R$ with the prime determined by $\mathfrak q$ and the chosen embedding. Its local ring is $S$, so it gives a common strict localization $T=\operatorname{Spec}R^{\mathrm{sh}}\simeq\operatorname{Spec}S^{\mathrm{sh}}$, with the same closed point $t$. In particular the complements of that closed point are the same scheme $T^\circ$. The identification respects both structural maps and their maximal ideals, not just the underlying abstract rings.

source.place: Expose XVI, after Definition 3.2.1 and Definition 3.2.2, printed p.244; detailed reconstruction of the strict-local argument

proof.text:
For either local scheme $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ or $\operatorname{Spec}S$, let $i:z\hookrightarrow V$ be its closed point and $j:V^\circ=V\setminus\{z\}\hookrightarrow V$. Apply [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] to $F=A_V(d)$ and shift by $2d$. On $D^+$ its $Ri^!$ is the fixed adjoint of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction] by uniqueness of right adjoints of $i_*$: for $K\in D^{\ge a}$ and $L\in D^{<a}$, $\operatorname{Hom}(L,Ri^!K)=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*L,K)=0$, so $Ri^!K\in D^{\ge a}$. Its total $Rj_*$ is the bounded-below one, as bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Take the geometric fibre at $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to z$; it is exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. The left term becomes $(i^!F[2d])_{\bar z}$, as $i^{-1}i_*=\mathrm{id}$ [lem-kun-04ca]. For the other terms use the canonical derived germ comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] for $\mathrm{id}_V$ and $j$, both qcqs ($V$ affine Noetherian). Their strict local scheme is $T$: [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] gives $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{V,\bar z}\cong R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ (resp. $S^{\mathrm{sh}}$) over $V$, inducing the identity of $k^s$, so $V^\circ\times_VT=T^\circ$. We get the distinguished triangle
$$(i^!A_V(d)[2d])_{\bar z}\to R\Gamma(T,A_T(d))[2d]\to R\Gamma(T^\circ,A_{T^\circ}(d))[2d]\to(i^!A_V(d)[2d])_{\bar z}[1],$$
whose middle arrow is restriction of sections. The stalk formula, stated for abelian sheaves, applies to the module objects: [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies the cohomology of module direct images of $F$ and $j^*F$ with the abelian ones in every degree, so the canonical germ morphisms are quasi-isomorphisms of $A$-module complexes. No adic or constructibility comparison is used.

source.place: Expose XVI, after Definition 3.2.1 and Definition 3.2.2, printed p.244; detailed reconstruction of the strict-local argument

proof.text: Apply the triangle calculation to both $V$'s. The common strict localization $T$ is a Noetherian regular local scheme of dimension $d$ [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian, lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular, lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension], so $t\hookrightarrow T$ is a regular closed immersion of codimension $d$ of Noetherian schemes and its class is defined; $T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $T\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ are affine ind-etale localizations of Noetherian pairs. The canonical supported continuity comparison therefore identifies their geometric closed-support objects with the same homotopy fibre of $R\Gamma(T,A_T(d))[2d]\to R\Gamma(T^\circ,A_{T^\circ}(d))[2d]$. Compare the maps as well as the objects. By [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], the closed-point class is the product of the supported Cartier Kummer classes of a regular system of parameters, is independent of those parameters, and commutes with localization and strict localization via these canonical supported continuity identifications. Thus the two geometric maps from $A$ to this common supported object are the same Kummer class (with the same sign). Equivalently their supported Ext representatives agree; transposition under the fixed adjunction of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction] gives exactly the maps defining purity in [def-per-punctual-purity]. Here the common dimension $d$ from step 1 is essential for both the twist and the shift. We do not replace either map by an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism.

source.place: Expose XVI, after Definition 3.2.1 and Definition 3.2.2, printed p.244; detailed reconstruction of the strict-local argument

proof.text: For a field $k$ and an algebraically closed overfield of its separable closure, [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] identifies the geometric stalk of an abelian etale sheaf with its underlying discrete Galois module. This stalk is exact and conservative: the equivalence is exact, and a bijective equivariant homomorphism has an equivariant inverse. Applied degreewise to complexes, exactness identifies cohomology with the stalk of cohomology; consequently a derived morphism is an isomorphism if and only if this one geometric fibre is a quasi-isomorphism. The same test applies to $A$-module sheaves, since kernels and cokernels vanish precisely when their underlying abelian sheaves vanish, and derived isomorphisms are detected on cohomology by [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The two purity maps have the same geometric fibre by step 3, so one is an isomorphism if and only if the other is. This proves the pointwise assertion for the original $x,y$, without an excellence hypothesis.

source.place: Expose XVI, after Definition 3.2.1 and Definition 3.2.2, printed p.244; detailed reconstruction of the strict-local argument

proof.text: If $X$ is punctually pure, the pointwise equivalence applied to each $Y_\alpha\to X$ proves purity at every point of every $Y_\alpha$. Conversely, given purity of all $Y_\alpha$ and $x\in X$, joint surjectivity supplies an $\alpha$ and $y\in Y_\alpha$ over $x$; the pointwise equivalence proves purity at $x$. Quantifying over $x$ proves the family assertion, with the predicates exactly as in [def-per-punctual-purity]. If $X$ is empty all assertions are vacuous, including the empty covering family.
